correctness.rationale: For each finite chain factor, annihilators are exactly valuation-determined ideals. The proof derives the ordered-comparable multiplicative count T and same-class multiplicative count Q, removes all unit/zero ordered pairs, and obtains exact edges. For incomparable vectors, common-neighbor analysis gives distance two except opposite Boolean valuation corners; constructive three-edge paths exist precisely outside the two-field disconnected boundary. Each complementary support pair has exactly U element pairs, producing D3=(2^{r-1}-1)U. A direct finite-ring BFS verifier passed 29 integer-residue rings, nine actual direct products and six nonprime residue-field valuation instances, including the eleven-vertex Z4×Z4 graph (30,21,4 distances); finite checks do not establish the arbitrary-factor result independently of the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper introduces the graph and proves only a connected-diameter upper bound four, giving an incorrect four for Z4×Z4. The 2012 full text explicitly introduces the complement-of-cozero graph but treats girth/cliques and structural questions, not the present full distance count; the 2019 scalar-product graph similarly identifies the complement as an induced graph without its metric distribution. The 2022 Wiener paper computes distances for the cozero graph itself, not its complementary graph. Relevant indexed records concern Badawi annihilator graphs, zero-divisor graphs, or other invariants. The claimed original contribution is the complete exact distance-enumerator and sharp principal-ideal-ring metric classification, not graph equivalence or the classical ring decomposition.
residual_risks: An exact complement-of-cozero distance enumeration may exist in older unindexed comparability-graph or ring-graph literature; no novelty claim is based solely on negative search results.
Secondary ring-graph papers and potentially inaccessible sources were not exhaustively read. Independent mathematical review has not occurred.

value.rationale: A complete metric census and Wiener polynomial for the natural annihilator-inclusion graph of every finite principal ideal ring addresses the diameter problem of Safari--Shaveisi--Nikandish 2026, sharply restricts the possible diameter, classifies the unique disconnected family, and gives a uniform factorized distance-three coefficient by complementary local supports. The result has intrinsic graph-index value beyond a single negative counterexample and supplies a self-contained exact benchmark across arbitrary chain lengths and residue-field orders.
